It leads with the batch number and the count, as the tag does. It is 4 words and 23 characters, inside the kit's 5-word, 32-character limit, and it adapts the kit's announcement sample line.

posts.goal: Teach the one thing stoneware doesn't like.
posts.details: Don't move a piece straight from the fridge to a hot oven; big temperature jumps can crack stoneware. Let it come to room temperature first.

slots.headline: Let it warm up first.
slots.subhead: Fridge to hot oven can crack stoneware. Let it reach room temperature.
slots.caption: Stoneware minds one thing: a big jump in temperature. Fridge straight to a hot oven can crack a piece, so let it come to room temperature first. Dishwasher safe, and made for daily use. #stoneware

notes.reason: The kit names type-led as the first choice for tips: one care instruction set large in serif. The brief gives no concrete reason to depart, since it is a single instruction and the instruction is the content.

Type-led takes no photo. None of the three photos shows the fridge-to-oven risk anyway. Photo 03's tag shows batch and price, which would add an unrelated offer message to a care tip. The kit also wants type on paper, not on images.

A short, calm declarative that gives the instruction itself. It is five words and 21 characters, inside the kit's 5-word limit, with no exclamation mark and no talk of fragility. This was kept from the earlier draft because the critique didn't flag it.

notes.choice: Fridge to hot oven can crack stoneware. Let it reach room temperature.
notes.reason: It adds the concrete detail the headline leaves out: which temperature jump to avoid and what to do instead. It uses only facts from the brief and stays within 80 characters. Kept unchanged.
The kit allows only one small label per post, for a batch number or a price. The brief has neither, and anything else would repeat the subhead.

notes.choice: Removed the 'hot coffee' line. The caption now says 'Dishwasher safe, and made for daily use.' and keeps the #stoneware hashtag.
notes.reason: This fixes the critique. Hot coffee is a heat-safety claim the kit doesn't support, and it sat oddly beside a post about temperature limits. Dishwasher safe and daily use are both stated in the kit. The caption is three sentences and under 350 characters, with one hashtag.

critique.summary: The type-led tip post teaches the brief's one instruction in calm, exact copy with no invented facts, and the render is clean: legible serif headline, no overlap or cut-off, no accent element, and the caption's only hashtag is the permitted #stoneware. Every automated check passes.

slots.headline: Fridge to hot oven? Never.
slots.subhead: Big temperature jumps can crack stoneware. Let it come to room temperature first.
slots.caption:
The one thing stoneware doesn't like is a sudden change in temperature. If a piece has been in the fridge, set it on the counter and let it come to room temperature before it goes into a hot oven. A little patience keeps your tableware in one piece.

#stoneware #ceramics #handmadetableware #portlandmaine

notes.reason: The brief is a tip with one instruction, and type-led is the template built for that: the instruction is the content. A photo would add nothing the words don't already say. Split also suits tips, but only with a photo that earns its half of the frame.

No photo shows the fridge-to-oven situation. The trimming shot shows unfired clay, which would confuse a care tip about finished stoneware. The tagged mug carries a price and batch number that would pull attention from the tip and could read as a sales post. The plates-by-window shot is pleasant but only decorative here.
States the single rule up front in a short, memorable line, which suits a type-led tip where the instruction is the content. It is well under the 40-character limit.

notes.choice: Reason plus fix in one sentence pair: big temperature jumps can crack stoneware, so let it come to room temperature first.
notes.reason: The headline gives the rule, so the subhead adds the why and the how, using only the facts in the brief. It is 80 characters, within the 90 limit.

slots.quote: I bought it for the shelf. It hasn't been on the shelf since.

#HollisWare #PortlandMaine #Stoneware #CeramicsStudio #EverydayCup
